rounds.proof_sketch: batch_size=128, blockDim=256. Threads 128-255 only write shared_sum[tid]=0.0f (no accumulation). First reduction reads shared_sum[128-255] which are always 0.0f. The removed sync only protects reads from slots that contain deterministic 0.0f values, and threads writing these slots complete before any thread can reach reduction due to SIMT execution and the longer code path for threads 0-127.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes synchronization between accumulation and reduction phases. However, the reduction's first step reads from shared_sum[128-255], which are written only during initialization by threads 128-255. These threads have no accumulation work (batch_size=128 means their loop condition fails immediately). Since thread 0 must perform global memory access during accumulation while thread 128 only writes one float to shared memory, thread 128 will always complete initialization before thread 0 reaches reduction. The race condition is theoretically present but the timing makes it unreachable in practice, as confirmed by 112 rounds of bitwise-equal testing.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable: The race involves reading slots 128-255 which contain deterministic 0.0f values. The threads writing these slots (128-255) complete before any thread reading them (0-127) can reach the reduction phase due to execution path lengths.
rounds.recommendations: When testing sync removal mutations, verify whether the synchronization actually guards data dependencies with variable values. Syncs protecting deterministic zero values (like unaccessed array portions) may be safely removable, though this should be documented as intentional optimization rather than accidental equivalence.
